units.leftText: “This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says to you, Baruch:
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah, the God of Israel, unto thee, O Baruch:

units.leftText: You have said, ‘Woe is me because the LORD has added sorrow to my pain! I am worn out with groaning and have found no rest.’”
units.rightText: Thou didst say, Woe is me now! for Jehovah hath added sorrow to my pain; I am weary with my groaning, and I find no rest.

units.leftText: Thus Jeremiah was to say to Baruch: “This is what the LORD says: Throughout the land I will demolish what I have built and uproot what I have planted.
units.rightText: Thus shalt thou say unto him, Thus saith Jehovah: Behold, that which I have built will I break down, and that which I have planted I will pluck up; and this in the whole land.
leftNotes: 45:4 Literally Thus you shall say to him:

units.leftText: But as for you, do you seek great things for yourself? Stop seeking! For I will bring disaster on every living creature, declares the LORD, but wherever you go, I will grant your life as a spoil of war.”
units.rightText: And seekest thou great things for thyself? seek them not; for, behold, I will bring evil upon all flesh, saith Jehovah; but thy life will I give unto thee for a prey in all places whither thou goest.

units.leftText: This is the word of the LORD about the nations— the word that came to Jeremiah the prophet
units.rightText: The word of Jehovah which came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the nations.

units.leftText: concerning Egypt and the army of Pharaoh Neco king of Egypt, which was defeated at Carchemish on the Euphrates River by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah king of Judah:
units.rightText: Of Egypt: concerning the army of Pharaoh-neco king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates in Carchemish, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote in the fourth year of Jehoiakim the son of Josiah, king of Judah.

units.leftText: “Deploy your shields, small and large; advance for battle!
units.rightText: Prepare ye the buckler and shield, and draw near to battle.

units.leftText: Harness the horses; mount the steeds; take your positions with helmets on! Polish your spears; put on armor!
units.rightText: Harness the horses, and get up, ye horsemen, and stand forth with your helmets; furbish the spears, put on the coats of mail.

units.leftText: Why am I seeing this? They are terrified, they are retreating; their warriors are defeated, they flee in haste without looking back; terror is on every side!” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: Wherefore have I seen it? they are dismayed and are turned backward; and their mighty ones are beaten down, and are fled apace, and look not back: terror is on every side, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “The swift cannot flee, and the warrior cannot escape! In the north by the River Euphrates they stumble and fall.
units.rightText: Let not the swift flee away, nor the mighty man escape; in the north by the river Euphrates have they stumbled and fallen.

units.leftText: Who is this, rising like the Nile, like rivers whose waters churn?
units.rightText: Who is this that riseth up like the Nile, whose waters toss themselves like the rivers?

units.leftText: Egypt rises like the Nile, and its waters churn like rivers, boasting, ‘I will rise and cover the earth; I will destroy the cities and their people.’
units.rightText: Egypt riseth up like the Nile, and his waters toss themselves like the rivers: and he saith, I will rise up, I will cover the earth; I will destroy cities and the inhabitants thereof.

units.leftText: Advance, O horses! Race furiously, O chariots! Let the warriors come forth— Cush and Put carrying their shields, men of Lydia drawing the bow.
units.rightText: Go up, ye horses; and rage, ye chariots; and let the mighty men go forth: Cush and Put, that handle the shield; and the Ludim, that handle and bend the bow.
leftNotes: 46:9 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: For that day belongs to the Lord GOD of Hosts, a day of vengeance against His foes. The sword will devour until it is satisfied, until it is quenched with their blood. For the Lord GOD of Hosts will hold a sacrifice in the land of the north by the River Euphrates.
units.rightText: For that day is a day of the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, a day of vengeance, that he may avenge him of his adversaries: and the sword shall devour and be satiate, and shall drink its fill of their blood; for the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, hath a sacrifice in the north country by the river Euphrates.

units.leftText: Go up to Gilead for balm, O Virgin Daughter of Egypt! In vain you try many remedies, but for you there is no healing.
units.rightText: Go up into Gilead, and take balm, O virgin daughter of Egypt: in vain dost thou use many medicines; there is no healing for thee.

units.leftText: The nations have heard of your shame, and your outcry fills the earth, because warrior stumbles over warrior and both of them have fallen together.”
units.rightText: The nations have heard of thy shame, and the earth is full of thy cry; for the mighty man hath stumbled against the mighty, they are fallen both of them together.

units.leftText: This is the word that the LORD spoke to Jeremiah the prophet about the coming of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon to strike the land of Egypt:
units.rightText: The word that Jehovah spake to Jeremiah the prophet, how that Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon should come and smite the land of Egypt.

units.leftText: “Announce it in Egypt, and proclaim it in Migdol; proclaim it in Memphis and Tahpanhes: ‘Take your positions and prepare yourself, for the sword devours those around you.’
units.rightText: Declare ye in Egypt, and publish in Migdol, and publish in Memphis and in Tahpanhes: say ye, Stand forth, and prepare thee; for the sword hath devoured round about thee.
leftNotes: 46:14 LXX; Hebrew Noph; also in verse 19

units.leftText: Why have your warriors been laid low? They cannot stand, for the LORD has thrust them down.
units.rightText: Why are thy strong ones swept away? they stood not, because Jehovah did drive them.

units.leftText: They continue to stumble; indeed, they have fallen over one another. They say, ‘Get up! Let us return to our people and to the land of our birth, away from the sword of the oppressor.’
units.rightText: He made many to stumble, yea, they fell one upon another: and they said, Arise, and let us go again to our own people, and to the land of our nativity, from the oppressing sword.

units.leftText: There they will cry out: ‘Pharaoh king of Egypt was all noise; he has let the appointed time pass him by.’
units.rightText: They cried there, Pharaoh king of Egypt is but a noise; he hath let the appointed time pass by.

units.leftText: As surely as I live, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts, there will come one who is like Tabor among the mountains and like Carmel by the sea.
units.rightText: As I live, saith the King, whose name is Jehovah of hosts, surely like Tabor among the mountains, and like Carmel by the sea, so shall he come.

units.leftText: Pack your bags for exile, O daughter dwelling in Egypt! For Memphis will be laid waste, destroyed and uninhabited.
units.rightText: O thou daughter that dwellest in Egypt, furnish thyself to go into captivity; for Memphis shall become a desolation, and shall be burnt up, without inhabitant.

units.leftText: Egypt is a beautiful heifer, but a gadfly from the north is coming against her.
units.rightText: Egypt is a very fair heifer; but destruction out of the north is come, it is come.

units.leftText: Even the mercenaries among her are like fattened calves. They too will turn back; together they will flee, they will not stand their ground, for the day of calamity is coming upon them — the time of their punishment.
units.rightText: Also her hired men in the midst of her are like calves of the stall; for they also are turned back, they are fled away together, they did not stand: for the day of their calamity is come upon them, the time of their visitation.

units.leftText: Egypt will hiss like a fleeing serpent, for the enemy will advance in force; with axes they will come against her like woodsmen cutting down trees.
units.rightText: The sound thereof shall go like the serpent; for they shall march with an army, and come against her with axes, as hewers of wood.
leftNotes: 46:22 Hebrew nachash; translated in most cases as snake

units.leftText: They will chop down her forest, declares the LORD, dense though it may be, for they are more numerous than locusts; they cannot be counted.
units.rightText: They shall cut down her forest, saith Jehovah, though it cannot be searched; because they are more than the locusts, and are innumerable.

units.leftText: The Daughter of Egypt will be put to shame; she will be delivered into the hands of the people of the north.”
units.rightText: The daughter of Egypt shall be put to shame; she shall be delivered into the hand of the people of the north.

units.leftText: The LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Behold, I am about to punish Amon god of Thebes, along with Pharaoh, Egypt with her gods and kings, and those who trust in Pharaoh.
units.rightText: Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel, saith: Behold, I will punish Amon of No, and Pharaoh, and Egypt, with her gods, and her kings; even Pharaoh, and them that trust in him:
leftNotes: 46:25 Hebrew Amon of No

units.leftText: I will deliver them into the hands of those who seek their lives— of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and his officers. But after this, Egypt will be inhabited as in days of old, declares the LORD.
units.rightText: and I will deliver them into the hand of those that seek their lives, and into the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, and into the hand of his servants; and afterwards it shall be inhabited, as in the days of old, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: But you, O Jacob My servant, do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed, O Israel. For I will surely save you out of a distant place, your descendants from the land of their captivity! Jacob will return to quiet and ease, with no one to make him afraid.
units.rightText: But fear not thou, O Jacob my servant, neither be dismayed, O Israel: for, lo, I will save thee from afar, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and shall be quiet and at ease, and none shall make him afraid.

units.leftText: And you, My servant Jacob, do not be afraid, declares the LORD, for I am with you. Though I will completely destroy all the nations to which I have banished you, I will not completely destroy you. Yet I will discipline you justly, and will by no means leave you unpunished.”
units.rightText: Fear not thou, O Jacob my servant, saith Jehovah; for I am with thee: for I will make a full end of all the nations whither I have driven thee; but I will not make a full end of thee, but I will correct thee in measure, and will in no wise leave thee unpunished.

units.leftText: This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet about the Philistines before Pharaoh struck down Gaza.
units.rightText: The word of Jehovah that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning the Philistines, before that Pharaoh smote Gaza.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “See how the waters are rising from the north and becoming an overflowing torrent. They will overflow the land and its fullness, the cities and their inhabitants. The people will cry out, and all who dwell in the land will wail
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah: Behold, waters rise up out of the north, and shall become an overflowing stream, and shall overflow the land and all that is therein, the city and them that dwell therein; and the men shall cry, and all the inhabitants of the land shall wail.

units.leftText: at the sound of the galloping hooves of stallions, the rumbling of chariots, and the clatter of their wheels. The fathers will not turn back for their sons; their hands will hang limp.
units.rightText: At the noise of the stamping of the hoofs of his strong ones, at the rushing of his chariots, at the rumbling of his wheels, the fathers look not back to their children for feebleness of hands;

units.leftText: For the day has come to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every remaining ally. Indeed, the LORD is about to destroy the Philistines, the remnant from the coasts of Caphtor.
units.rightText: because of the day that cometh to destroy all the Philistines, to cut off from Tyre and Sidon every helper that remaineth: for Jehovah will destroy the Philistines, the remnant of the isle of Caphtor.
leftNotes: 47:4 That is, Crete

units.leftText: The people of Gaza will shave their heads in mourning; Ashkelon will be silenced. O remnant of their valley, how long will you gash yourself?
units.rightText: Baldness is come upon Gaza; Ashkelon is brought to nought, the remnant of their valley: how long wilt thou cut thyself?
leftNotes: 47:5 That is, the Mediterranean coast or plain

units.leftText: ‘Alas, O sword of the LORD, how long until you rest? Return to your sheath; cease and be still!’
units.rightText: O thou sword of Jehovah, how long will it be ere thou be quiet? put up thyself into thy scabbard; rest, and be still.

units.leftText: How can it rest when the LORD has commanded it? He has appointed it against Ashkelon and the shore of its coastland.”
units.rightText: How canst thou be quiet, seeing Jehovah hath given thee a charge? Against Ashkelon, and against the sea-shore, there hath he appointed it.

units.leftText: Concerning Moab, this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “Woe to Nebo, for it will be devastated. Kiriathaim will be captured and disgraced; the fortress will be shattered and dismantled.
units.rightText: Of Moab. Thus saith Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel: Woe unto Nebo! for it is laid waste; Kiriathaim is put to shame, it is taken; Misgab is put to shame and broken down.

units.leftText: There is no longer praise for Moab; in Heshbon they devise evil against her: ‘Come, let us cut her off from nationhood.’ You too, O people of Madmen, will be silenced; the sword will pursue you.
units.rightText: The praise of Moab is no more; in Heshbon they have devised evil against her: Come, and let us cut her off from being a nation. Thou also, O Madmen, shalt be brought to silence; the sword shall pursue thee.
leftNotes: 48:2 The Hebrew for Heshbon sounds like the Hebrew for plot.
48:2 The name of the Moabite town Madmen sounds like the Hebrew for silenced.

units.leftText: A voice cries out from Horonaim: ‘Devastation and great destruction!’
units.rightText: The sound of a cry from Horonaim, desolation and great destruction!

units.leftText: Moab will be shattered; her little ones will cry out.
units.rightText: Moab is destroyed; her little ones have caused a cry to be heard.
leftNotes: 48:4 Hebrew; LXX her cries are heard as far away as Zoar

units.leftText: For on the ascent to Luhith they weep bitterly as they go, and on the descent to Horonaim cries of distress resound over the destruction:
units.rightText: For by the ascent of Luhith with continual weeping shall they go up; for at the descent of Horonaim they have heard the distress of the cry of destruction.

units.leftText: ‘Flee! Run for your lives! Become like a juniper in the desert. ’
units.rightText: Flee, save your lives, and be like the heath in the wilderness.
leftNotes: 48:6 Or like a wild donkey or like Aroer

units.leftText: Because you trust in your works and treasures, you too will be captured, and Chemosh will go into exile with his priests and officials.
units.rightText: For, because thou hast trusted in thy works and in thy treasures, thou also shalt be taken: and Chemosh shall go forth into captivity, his priests and his princes together.

units.leftText: The destroyer will move against every city, and not one town will escape. The valley will also be ruined, and the high plain will be destroyed, as the LORD has said.
units.rightText: And the destroyer shall come upon every city, and no city shall escape; the valley also shall perish, and the plain shall be destroyed; as Jehovah hath spoken.

units.leftText: Put salt on Moab, for she will be laid waste; her cities will become desolate, with no one to dwell in them.
units.rightText: Give wings unto Moab, that she may fly and get her away: and her cities shall become a desolation, without any to dwell therein.
leftNotes: 48:9 Or Give wings to Moab, for she would fly away

units.leftText: Cursed is the one who is remiss in doing the work of the LORD, and cursed is he who withholds his sword from bloodshed.
units.rightText: Cursed be he that doeth the work of Jehovah negligently; and cursed be he that keepeth back his sword from blood.

units.leftText: Moab has been at ease from youth, settled like wine on its dregs; he has not been poured from vessel to vessel or gone into exile. So his flavor has remained the same, and his aroma is unchanged.
units.rightText: Moab hath been at ease from his youth, and he hath settled on his lees, and hath not been emptied from vessel to vessel, neither hath he gone into captivity: therefore his taste remaineth in him, and his scent is not changed.

units.leftText: Therefore behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will send to him wanderers, who will pour him out. They will empty his vessels and shatter his jars.
units.rightText: Therefore, behold, the days come, saith Jehovah, that I will send unto him them that pour off, and they shall pour him off; and they shall empty his vessels, and break their bottles in pieces.

units.leftText: Then Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, just as the house of Israel was ashamed when they trusted in Bethel.
units.rightText: And Moab shall be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Beth-el their confidence.

units.leftText: How can you say, ‘We are warriors, mighty men ready for battle’ ?
units.rightText: How say ye, We are mighty men, and valiant men for the war?

units.leftText: Moab has been destroyed and its towns have been invaded; the best of its young men have gone down in the slaughter, declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: Moab is laid waste, and they are gone up into his cities, and his chosen young men are gone down to the slaughter, saith the King, whose name is Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: Moab’s calamity is at hand, and his affliction is rushing swiftly.
units.rightText: The calamity of Moab is near to come, and his affliction hasteth fast.

units.leftText: Mourn for him, all you who surround him, everyone who knows his name; tell how the mighty scepter is shattered — the glorious staff!
units.rightText: All ye that are round about him, bemoan him, and all ye that know his name; say, How is the strong staff broken, the beautiful rod!

units.leftText: Come down from your glory; sit on parched ground, O daughter dwelling in Dibon, for the destroyer of Moab has come against you; he has destroyed your fortresses.
units.rightText: O thou daughter that dwellest in Dibon, come down from thy glory, and sit in thirst; for the destroyer of Moab is come up against thee, he hath destroyed thy strongholds.

units.leftText: Stand by the road and watch, O dweller of Aroer! Ask the man fleeing or the woman escaping, ‘What has happened?’
units.rightText: O inhabitant of Aroer, stand by the way, and watch: ask him that fleeth, and her that escapeth; say, What hath been done?

units.leftText: Moab is put to shame, for it has been shattered. Wail and cry out! Declare by the Arnon that Moab is destroyed.
units.rightText: Moab is put to shame; for it is broken down: wail and cry; tell ye it by the Arnon, that Moab is laid waste.

units.leftText: Judgment has come upon the high plain— upon Holon, Jahzah, and Mephaath,
units.rightText: And judgment is come upon the plain country, upon Holon, and upon Jahzah, and upon Mephaath,
leftNotes: 48:21 Jahzah is a variant of Jahaz; see verse 34.

units.leftText: upon Dibon, Nebo, and Beth-diblathaim,
units.rightText: and upon Dibon, and upon Nebo, and upon Beth-diblathaim,

units.leftText: upon Kiriathaim, Beth-gamul, and Beth-meon,
units.rightText: and upon Kiriathaim, and upon Beth-gamul, and upon Beth-meon,

units.leftText: upon Kerioth, Bozrah, and all the towns of Moab, those far and near.
units.rightText: and upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah, and upon all the cities of the land of Moab, far or near.

units.leftText: The horn of Moab has been cut off, and his arm is broken,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arm is broken, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Make him drunk, because he has magnified himself against the LORD; so Moab will wallow in his own vomit, and he will also become a laughingstock.
units.rightText: Make ye him drunken; for he magnified himself against Jehovah: and Moab shall wallow in his vomit, and he also shall be in derision.

units.leftText: Was not Israel your object of ridicule? Was he ever found among thieves? For whenever you speak of him you shake your head.
units.rightText: For was not Israel a derision unto thee? was he found among thieves? for as often as thou speakest of him, thou waggest the head.

units.leftText: Abandon the towns and settle among the rocks, O dwellers of Moab! Be like a dove that nests at the mouth of a cave.
units.rightText: O ye inhabitants of Moab, leave the cities, and dwell in the rock; and be like the dove that maketh her nest over the mouth of the abyss.

units.leftText: We have heard of Moab’s pomposity, his exceeding pride and conceit, his proud arrogance and haughtiness of heart.
units.rightText: We have heard of the pride of Moab, that he is very proud; his loftiness, and his pride, and his arrogancy, and the haughtiness of his heart.

units.leftText: I know his insolence,” declares the LORD, “but it is futile. His boasting is as empty as his deeds.
units.rightText: I know his wrath, saith Jehovah, that it is nought; his boastings have wrought nothing.

units.leftText: Therefore I will wail for Moab; I will cry out for all of Moab; I will moan for the men of Kir-heres.
units.rightText: Therefore will I wail for Moab; yea, I will cry out for all Moab: for the men of Kir-heres shall they mourn.
leftNotes: 48:31 Kir-heres is a variant of Kir-hareseth; also in verse 36; see Isaiah 16:7|ISA 16:7*.

units.leftText: I will weep for you, O vine of Sibmah, more than I weep for Jazer. Your tendrils have extended to the sea; they reach even to Jazer. The destroyer has descended on your summer fruit and grape harvest.
units.rightText: With more than the weeping of Jazer will I weep for thee, O vine of Sibmah: thy branches passed over the sea, they reached even to the sea of Jazer: upon thy summer fruits and upon thy vintage the destroyer is fallen.
leftNotes: 48:32 Probably the Dead Sea
48:32 Two Hebrew manuscripts and LXX; most Hebrew manuscripts to the Sea of Jazer

units.leftText: Joy and gladness are removed from the orchard and from the fields of Moab. I have stopped the flow of wine from the presses; no one treads them with shouts of joy; their shouts are not for joy.
units.rightText: And gladness and joy is taken away from the fruitful field and from the land of Moab; and I have caused wine to cease from the winepresses: none shall tread with shouting; the shouting shall be no shouting.

units.leftText: There is a cry from Heshbon to Elealeh; they raise their voices to Jahaz, from Zoar to Horonaim and Eglath-shelishiyah; for even the waters of Nimrim have dried up.
units.rightText: From the cry of Heshbon even unto Elealeh, even unto Jahaz have they uttered their voice, from Zoar even unto Horonaim, to Eglath-shelishiyah: for the waters of Nimrim also shall become desolate.

units.leftText: In Moab, declares the LORD, I will bring an end to those who make offerings on the high places and burn incense to their gods.
units.rightText: Moreover I will cause to cease in Moab, saith Jehovah, him that offereth in the high place, and him that burneth incense to his gods.

units.leftText: Therefore My heart laments like a flute for Moab; it laments like a flute for the men of Kir-heres, because the wealth they acquired has perished.
units.rightText: Therefore my heart soundeth for Moab like pipes, and my heart soundeth like pipes for the men of Kir-heres: therefore the abundance that he hath gotten is perished.

units.leftText: For every head is shaved and every beard is clipped; on every hand is a gash, and around every waist is sackcloth.
units.rightText: For every head is bald, and every beard clipped: upon all the hands are cuttings, and upon the loins sackcloth.

units.leftText: On all the rooftops of Moab and in the public squares, everyone is mourning; for I have shattered Moab like an unwanted jar,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: On all the housetops of Moab and in the streets thereof there is lamentation every where; for I have broken Moab like a vessel wherein none delighteth, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “How shattered it is! How they wail! How Moab has turned his back in shame! Moab has become an object of ridicule and horror to all those around him.”
units.rightText: How is it broken down! how do they wail! how hath Moab turned the back with shame! so shall Moab become a derision and a terror to all that are round about him.

units.leftText: For this is what the LORD says: “Behold, an eagle swoops down and spreads his wings against Moab.
units.rightText: For thus saith Jehovah: Behold, he shall fly as an eagle, and shall spread out his wings against Moab.

units.leftText: Kirioth has been taken, and the strongholds seized. In that day the heart of Moab’s warriors will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
units.rightText: Kerioth is taken, and the strongholds are seized, and the heart of the mighty men of Moab at that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.

units.leftText: Moab will be destroyed as a nation because he vaunted himself against the LORD.
units.rightText: And Moab shall be destroyed from being a people, because he hath magnified himself against Jehovah.

units.leftText: Terror and pit and snare await you, O dweller of Moab,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: Fear, and the pit, and the snare, are upon thee, O inhabitant of Moab, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Whoever flees the panic will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs from the pit will be caught in the snare. For I will bring upon Moab the year of their punishment,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: He that fleeth from the fear shall fall into the pit; and he that getteth up out of the pit shall be taken in the snare: for I will bring upon him, even upon Moab, the year of their visitation, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Those who flee will stand helpless in Heshbon’s shadow, because fire has gone forth from Heshbon and a flame from within Sihon. It devours the foreheads of Moab and the skulls of the sons of tumult.
units.rightText: They that fled stand without strength under the shadow of Heshbon; for a fire is gone forth out of Heshbon, and a flame from the midst of Sihon, and hath devoured the corner of Moab, and the crown of the head of the tumultuous ones.

units.leftText: Woe to you, O Moab! The people of Chemosh have perished; for your sons have been taken into exile and your daughters have gone into captivity.
units.rightText: Woe unto thee, O Moab! the people of Chemosh is undone; for thy sons are taken away captive, and thy daughters into captivity.

units.leftText: Yet in the latter days I will restore Moab from captivity, ” declares the LORD. Here ends the judgment on Moab.
units.rightText: Yet will I bring back the captivity of Moab in the latter days, saith Jehovah. Thus far is the judgment of Moab.
leftNotes: 48:47 Or restore the fortunes of Moab

units.leftText: Concerning the Ammonites, this is what the LORD says: “Has Israel no sons? Is he without heir? Why then has Milcom taken possession of Gad? Why have his people settled in their cities?
units.rightText: Of the children of Ammon. Thus saith Jehovah: Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth Malcam possess Gad, and his people dwell in the cities thereof?
leftNotes: 49:1 Or their king; Milcom is a variant of Molech; also in verse 3; see Leviticus 18:21|LEV 18:21* and 1 Kings 11:7.

units.leftText: Therefore, behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will sound the battle cry against Rabbah of the Ammonites. It will become a heap of ruins, and its villages will be burned. Then Israel will drive out their dispossessors, says the LORD.
units.rightText: Therefore, behold, the days come, saith Jehovah, that I will cause an alarm of war to be heard against Rabbah of the children of Ammon; and it shall become a desolate heap, and her daughters shall be burned with fire: then shall Israel possess them that did possess him, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: Wail, O Heshbon, for Ai has been destroyed; cry out, O daughters of Rabbah! Put on sackcloth and mourn; run back and forth within your walls, for Milcom will go into exile together with his priests and officials.
units.rightText: Wail, O Heshbon, for Ai is laid waste; cry, ye daughters of Rabbah, gird you with sackcloth: lament, and run to and fro among the fences; for Malcam shall go into captivity, his priests and his princes together.

units.leftText: Why do you boast of your valleys— your valleys so fruitful, O faithless daughter? You trust in your riches and say, ‘Who can come against me?’
units.rightText: Wherefore gloriest thou in the valleys, thy flowing valley, O backsliding daughter? that trusted in her treasures, saying, Who shall come unto me?
leftNotes: 49:4 Or your valleys flowing

units.leftText: Behold, I am about to bring terror upon you, declares the Lord GOD of Hosts, from all those around you. You will each be driven headlong, with no one to regather the fugitives.
units.rightText: Behold, I will bring a fear upon thee, saith the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, from all that are round about thee; and ye shall be driven out every man right forth, and there shall be none to gather together the fugitives.

units.leftText: Yet afterward I will restore the Ammonites from captivity, ” declares the LORD. Judgment on Edom (Obadiah 1:1–14|OBA 1-14*)
units.rightText: But afterward I will bring back the captivity of the children of Ammon, saith Jehovah.
leftNotes: 49:6 Or restore the fortunes of the Ammonites

units.leftText: Concerning Edom, this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Is there no longer wisdom in Teman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom decayed?
units.rightText: Of Edom. Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: Is wisdom no more in Teman? is counsel perished from the prudent? is their wisdom vanished?

units.leftText: Turn and run! Lie low, O dwellers of Dedan, for I will bring disaster on Esau at the time I punish him.
units.rightText: Flee ye, turn back, dwell in the depths, O inhabitants of Dedan; for I will bring the calamity of Esau upon him, the time that I shall visit him.

units.leftText: If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings? Were thieves to come in the night, would they not steal only what they wanted?
units.rightText: If grape-gatherers came to thee, would they not leave some gleaning grapes? if thieves by night, would they not destroy till they had enough?

units.leftText: But I will strip Esau bare; I will uncover his hiding places, and he will be unable to conceal himself. His descendants will be destroyed along with his relatives and neighbors, and he will be no more.
units.rightText: But I have made Esau bare, I have uncovered his secret places, and he shall not be able to hide himself: his seed is destroyed, and his brethren, and his neighbors; and he is not.

units.leftText: Abandon your orphans; I will preserve their lives. Let your widows trust in Me.”
units.rightText: Leave thy fatherless children, I will preserve them alive; and let thy widows trust in me.

units.leftText: For this is what the LORD says: “If those who do not deserve to drink the cup must drink it, can you possibly remain unpunished? You will not go unpunished, for you must drink it too.
units.rightText: For thus saith Jehovah: Behold, they to whom it pertained not to drink of the cup shall assuredly drink; and art thou he that shall altogether go unpunished? thou shalt not go unpunished, but thou shalt surely drink.

units.leftText: For by Myself I have sworn, declares the LORD, that Bozrah will become a desolation, a disgrace, a ruin, and a curse, and all her cities will be in ruins forever.”
units.rightText: For I have sworn by myself, saith Jehovah, that Bozrah shall become an astonishment, a reproach, a waste, and a curse; and all the cities thereof shall be perpetual wastes.

units.leftText: I have heard a message from the LORD; an envoy has been sent to the nations: “Assemble yourselves to march against her! Rise up for battle!”
units.rightText: I have heard tidings from Jehovah, and an ambassador is sent among the nations, saying, Gather yourselves together, and come against her, and rise up to the battle.

units.leftText: “For behold, I will make you small among nations, despised among men.
units.rightText: For, behold, I have made thee small among the nations, and despised among men.

units.leftText: The terror you cause and the pride of your heart have deceived you, O dwellers in the clefts of the rocks, O occupiers of the mountain summit. Though you elevate your nest like the eagle, even from there I will bring you down,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: As for thy terribleness, the pride of thy heart hath deceived thee, O thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock, that holdest the height of the hill: though thou shouldest make thy nest as high as the eagle, I will bring thee down from thence, saith Jehovah.
leftNotes: 49:16 Or of Sela

units.leftText: “Edom will become an object of horror. All who pass by will be appalled and will scoff at all her wounds.
units.rightText: And Edom shall become an astonishment: every one that passeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss at all the plagues thereof.

units.leftText: As Sodom and Gomorrah were overthrown along with their neighbors,” says the LORD, “no one will dwell there; no man will abide there.
units.rightText: As in the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbor cities thereof, saith Jehovah, no man shall dwell there, neither shall any son of man sojourn therein.

units.leftText: Behold, one will come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan to the watered pasture. For in an instant I will chase Edom from her land. Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this? For who is like Me, and who can challenge Me? What shepherd can stand against Me?”
units.rightText: Behold, he shall come up like a lion from the pride of the Jordan against the strong habitation: for I will suddenly make them run away from it; and whoso is chosen, him will I appoint over it: for who is like me? and who will appoint me a time? and who is the shepherd that will stand before me?

units.leftText: Therefore hear the plans that the LORD has drawn up against Edom and the strategies He has devised against the people of Teman: Surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; certainly their pasture will be made desolate because of them.
units.rightText: Therefore hear ye the counsel of Jehovah, that he hath taken against Edom; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the inhabitants of Teman: Surely they shall drag them away, even the little ones of the flock; surely he shall make their habitation desolate over them.
leftNotes: 49:20 Or their pasture will be appalled at their fate

units.leftText: At the sound of their fall the earth will quake; their cry will resound to the Red Sea.
units.rightText: The earth trembleth at the noise of their fall; there is a cry, the noise whereof is heard in the Red Sea.
leftNotes: 49:21 Or the Sea of Reeds

units.leftText: Look! An eagle will soar and swoop down, spreading its wings over Bozrah. In that day the hearts of Edom’s mighty men will be like the heart of a woman in labor. Judgment on Damascus (Isaiah 17:1–14|ISA 17:1-14*)
units.rightText: Behold, he shall come up and fly as the eagle, and spread out his wings against Bozrah: and the heart of the mighty men of Edom at that day shall be as the heart of a woman in her pangs.

units.leftText: Concerning Damascus: “Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, for they have heard a bad report; they are agitated like the sea; their anxiety cannot be calmed.
units.rightText: Of Damascus. Hamath is confounded, and Arpad; for they have heard evil tidings, they are melted away: there is sorrow on the sea; it cannot be quiet.
leftNotes: 49:23 Hebrew on the sea or by the sea

units.leftText: Damascus has become feeble; she has turned to flee. Panic has gripped her; anguish and pain have seized her like a woman in labor.
units.rightText: Damascus is waxed feeble, she turneth herself to flee, and trembling hath seized on her: anguish and sorrows have taken hold of her, as of a woman in travail.

units.leftText: How is the city of praise not forsaken, the town that brings Me joy?
units.rightText: How is the city of praise not forsaken, the city of my joy?

units.leftText: For her young men will fall in the streets, and all her warriors will be silenced in that day,” declares the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: Therefore her young men shall fall in her streets, and all the men of war shall be brought to silence in that day, saith Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: “I will set fire to the walls of Damascus; it will consume the fortresses of Ben-hadad.” Judgment on Kedar and Hazor
units.rightText: And I will kindle a fire in the wall of Damascus, and it shall devour the palaces of Ben-hadad.

units.leftText: Concerning Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon defeated, this is what the LORD says: “Rise up, advance against Kedar, and destroy the people of the east!
units.rightText: Of Kedar, and of the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon smote. Thus saith Jehovah: Arise ye, go up to Kedar, and destroy the children of the east.

units.leftText: They will take their tents and flocks, their tent curtains and all their goods. They will take their camels for themselves. They will shout to them: ‘Terror is on every side!’
units.rightText: Their tents and their flocks shall they take; they shall carry away for themselves their curtains, and all their vessels, and their camels; and they shall cry unto them, Terror on every side!

units.leftText: Run! Escape quickly! Lie low, O residents of Hazor,” declares the LORD, “for Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has drawn up a plan against you; he has devised a strategy against you.
units.rightText: Flee ye, wander far off, dwell in the depths, O ye inhabitants of Hazor, saith Jehovah; for Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath taken counsel against you, and hath conceived a purpose against you.

units.leftText: Rise up, advance against a nation at ease, one that dwells securely,” declares the LORD. “They have no gates or bars; they live alone.
units.rightText: Arise, get you up unto a nation that is at ease, that dwelleth without care, saith Jehovah; that have neither gates nor bars, that dwell alone.

units.leftText: Their camels will become plunder, and their large herds will be spoil. I will scatter to the wind in every direction those who shave their temples; I will bring calamity on them from all sides,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: And their camels shall be a booty, and the multitude of their cattle a spoil: and I will scatter unto all winds them that have the corners of their hair cut off; and I will bring their calamity from every side of them, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Hazor will become a haunt for jackals, a desolation forever. No one will dwell there; no man will abide there.” Judgment on Elam
units.rightText: And Hazor shall be a dwelling-place of jackals, a desolation for ever: no man shall dwell there, neither shall any son of man sojourn therein.
leftNotes: 49:33 Or serpents or dragons

units.leftText: This is the word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah.
units.rightText: The word of Jehovah that came to Jeremiah the prophet concerning Elam, in the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, saying,

units.leftText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Behold, I will shatter Elam’s bow, the mainstay of their might.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: Behold, I will break the bow of Elam, the chief of their might.

units.leftText: I will bring the four winds against Elam from the four corners of the heavens, and I will scatter them to all these winds. There will not be a nation to which Elam’s exiles will not go.
units.rightText: And upon Elam will I bring the four winds from the four quarters of heaven, and will scatter them toward all those winds; and there shall be no nation whither the outcasts of Elam shall not come.

units.leftText: So I will shatter Elam before their foes, before those who seek their lives. I will bring disaster upon them, even My fierce anger,” declares the LORD. “I will send out the sword after them until I finish them off.
units.rightText: And I will cause Elam to be dismayed before their enemies, and before them that seek their life; and I will bring evil upon them, even my fierce anger, saith Jehovah; and I will send the sword after them, till I have consumed them:

units.leftText: I will set My throne in Elam, and destroy its king and officials,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: and I will set my throne in Elam, and will destroy from thence king and princes, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Yet in the last days, I will restore Elam from captivity, ” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: But it shall come to pass in the latter days, that I will bring back the captivity of Elam, saith Jehovah.
leftNotes: 49:39 Or restore the fortunes of Elam

units.leftText: This is the word that the LORD spoke through Jeremiah the prophet concerning Babylon and the land of the Chaldeans:
units.rightText: The word that Jehovah spake concerning Babylon, concerning the land of the Chaldeans, by Jeremiah the prophet.
leftNotes: 50:1 That is, the Babylonians; also in verses 8, 25, 35, and 45

units.leftText: “Announce and declare to the nations; lift up a banner and proclaim it; hold nothing back when you say, ‘Babylon is captured; Bel is put to shame; Marduk is shattered, her images are disgraced, her idols are broken in pieces.’
units.rightText: Declare ye among the nations and publish, and set up a standard; publish, and conceal not: say, Babylon is taken, Bel is put to shame, Merodach is dismayed; her images are put to shame, her idols are dismayed.

units.leftText: For a nation from the north will come against her; it will make her land a desolation. No one will live in it; both man and beast will flee.” Hope for Israel and Judah
units.rightText: For out of the north there cometh up a nation against her, which shall make her land desolate, and none shall dwell therein: they are fled, they are gone, both man and beast.

units.leftText: “In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, the children of Israel and the children of Judah will come together, weeping as they come, and will seek the LORD their God.
units.rightText: In those days, and in that time, saith Jehovah, the children of Israel shall come, they and the children of Judah together; they shall go on their way weeping, and shall seek Jehovah their God.

units.leftText: They will ask the way to Zion and turn their faces toward it. They will come and join themselves to the LORD in an everlasting covenant that will never be forgotten.
units.rightText: They shall inquire concerning Zion with their faces thitherward, saying, Come ye, and join yourselves to Jehovah in an everlasting covenant that shall not be forgotten.

units.leftText: My people are lost sheep; their shepherds have led them astray, causing them to roam the mountains. They have wandered from mountain to hill; they have forgotten their resting place.
units.rightText: My people have been lost sheep: their shepherds have caused them to go astray; they have turned them away on the mountains; they have gone from mountain to hill; they have forgotten their resting-place.

units.leftText: All who found them devoured them, and their enemies said, ‘We are not guilty, for they have sinned against the LORD, their true pasture, the LORD, the hope of their fathers.’
units.rightText: All that found them have devoured them; and their adversaries said, We are not guilty, because they have sinned against Jehovah, the habitation of righteousness, even Jehovah, the hope of their fathers.

units.leftText: Flee from the midst of Babylon; depart from the land of the Chaldeans; be like the he-goats that lead the flock.
units.rightText: Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and go forth out of the land of the Chaldeans, and be as the he-goats before the flocks.

units.leftText: For behold, I stir up and bring against Babylon an assembly of great nations from the land of the north. They will line up against her; from the north she will be captured. Their arrows will be like skilled warriors who do not return empty-handed.
units.rightText: For, lo, I will stir up and cause to come up against Babylon a company of great nations from the north country; and they shall set themselves in array against her; from thence she shall be taken: their arrows shall be as of an expert mighty man; none shall return in vain.

units.leftText: Chaldea will be plundered; all who plunder her will have their fill,” declares the LORD. Babylon’s Fall Is Certain
units.rightText: And Chaldea shall be a prey: all that prey upon her shall be satisfied, saith Jehovah.
leftNotes: 50:10 Or Babylonia

units.leftText: “Because you rejoice, because you sing in triumph— you who plunder My inheritance— because you frolic like a heifer treading grain and neigh like stallions,
units.rightText: Because ye are glad, because ye rejoice, O ye that plunder my heritage, because ye are wanton as a heifer that treadeth out the grain, and neigh as strong horses;

units.leftText: your mother will be greatly ashamed; she who bore you will be disgraced. Behold, she will be the least of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.
units.rightText: your mother shall be utterly put to shame; she that bare you shall be confounded: behold, she shall be the hindermost of the nations, a wilderness, a dry land, and a desert.

units.leftText: Because of the wrath of the LORD, she will not be inhabited; she will become completely desolate. All who pass through Babylon will be horrified and will hiss at all her wounds.
units.rightText: Because of the wrath of Jehovah she shall not be inhabited, but she shall be wholly desolate: every one that goeth by Babylon shall be astonished, and hiss at all her plagues.

units.leftText: Line up in formation around Babylon, all you who draw the bow! Shoot at her! Spare no arrows! For she has sinned against the LORD.
units.rightText: Set yourselves in array against Babylon round about, all ye that bend the bow; shoot at her, spare no arrows: for she hath sinned against Jehovah.

units.leftText: Raise a war cry against her on every side! She has thrown up her hands in surrender; her towers have fallen; her walls are torn down. Since this is the vengeance of the LORD, take out your vengeance upon her; as she has done, do the same to her.
units.rightText: Shout against her round about: she hath submitted herself; her bulwarks are fallen, her walls are thrown down; for it is the vengeance of Jehovah: take vengeance upon her; as she hath done, do unto her.

units.leftText: Cut off the sower from Babylon, and the one who wields the sickle at harvest time. In the face of the oppressor’s sword, each will turn to his own people, each will flee to his own land. Redemption for God’s People
units.rightText: Cut off the sower from Babylon, and him that handleth the sickle in the time of harvest: for fear of the oppressing sword they shall turn every one to his people, and they shall flee every one to his own land.

units.leftText: Israel is a scattered flock, chased away by lions. The first to devour him was the king of Assyria; the last to crush his bones was Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.”
units.rightText: Israel is a hunted sheep; the lions have driven him away: first, the king of Assyria devoured him; and now at last Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon hath broken his bones.

units.leftText: Therefore this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “I will punish the king of Babylon and his land as I punished the king of Assyria.
units.rightText: Therefore thus saith Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will punish the king of Babylon and his land, as I have punished the king of Assyria.

units.leftText: I will return Israel to his pasture, and he will graze on Carmel and Bashan; his soul will be satisfied on the hills of Ephraim and Gilead.
units.rightText: And I will bring Israel again to his pasture, and he shall feed on Carmel and Bashan, and his soul shall be satisfied upon the hills of Ephraim and in Gilead.

units.leftText: In those days and at that time, declares the LORD, a search will be made for Israel’s guilt, but there will be none, and for Judah’s sins, but they will not be found; for I will forgive the remnant I preserve. The Destruction of Babylon
units.rightText: In those days, and in that time, saith Jehovah, the iniquity of Israel shall be sought for, and there shall be none; and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found: for I will pardon them whom I leave as a remnant.

units.leftText: Go up against the land of Merathaim, and against the residents of Pekod. Kill them and devote them to destruction. Do all that I have commanded you,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: Go up against the land of Merathaim, even against it, and against the inhabitants of Pekod: slay and utterly destroy after them, saith Jehovah, and do according to all that I have commanded thee.
leftNotes: 50:21 LXX Avenge, O sword,
50:21 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering; also in verse 26.

units.leftText: “The noise of battle is in the land — the noise of great destruction.
units.rightText: A sound of battle is in the land, and of great destruction.

units.leftText: How the hammer of the whole earth lies broken and shattered! What a horror Babylon has become among the nations!
units.rightText: How is the hammer of the whole earth cut asunder and broken! how is Babylon become a desolation among the nations!

units.leftText: I laid a snare for you, O Babylon, and you were caught before you knew it. You were found and captured because you challenged the LORD.
units.rightText: I have laid a snare for thee, and thou art also taken, O Babylon, and thou wast not aware: thou art found, and also caught, because thou hast striven against Jehovah.

units.leftText: The LORD has opened His armory and brought out His weapons of wrath, for this is the work of the Lord GOD of Hosts in the land of the Chaldeans.
units.rightText: Jehovah hath opened his armory, and hath brought forth the weapons of his indignation; for the Lord, Jehovah of hosts, hath a work to do in the land of the Chaldeans.

units.leftText: Come against her from the farthest border. Break open her granaries; pile her up like mounds of grain. Devote her to destruction; leave her no survivors.
units.rightText: Come against her from the utmost border; open her store-houses; cast her up as heaps, and destroy her utterly; let nothing of her be left.

units.leftText: Kill all her young bulls; let them go down to the slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come — the time of their punishment.
units.rightText: Slay all her bullocks; let them go down to the slaughter: woe unto them! for their day is come, the time of their visitation.

units.leftText: Listen to the fugitives and refugees from the land of Babylon, declaring in Zion the vengeance of the LORD our God, the vengeance for His temple.
units.rightText: The voice of them that flee and escape out of the land of Babylon, to declare in Zion the vengeance of Jehovah our God, the vengeance of his temple.

units.leftText: Summon the archers against Babylon, all who string the bow. Encamp all around her; let no one escape. Repay her according to her deeds; do to her as she has done. For she has defied the LORD, the Holy One of Israel.
units.rightText: Call together the archers against Babylon, all them that bend the bow; encamp against her round about; let none thereof escape: recompense her according to her work; according to all that she hath done, do unto her; for she hath been proud against Jehovah, against the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: Therefore, her young men will fall in the streets, and all her warriors will be silenced in that day,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: Therefore shall her young men fall in her streets, and all her men of war shall be brought to silence in that day, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Behold, I am against you, O arrogant one,” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts, “for your day has come, the time when I will punish you.
units.rightText: Behold, I am against thee, O thou proud one, saith the Lord, Jehovah of hosts; for thy day is come, the time that I will visit thee.

units.leftText: The arrogant one will stumble and fall with no one to pick him up. And I will kindle a fire in his cities to consume all those around him.”
units.rightText: And the proud one shall stumble and fall, and none shall raise him up; and I will kindle a fire in his cities, and it shall devour all that are round about him.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “The sons of Israel are oppressed, and the sons of Judah as well. All their captors hold them fast, refusing to release them.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: The children of Israel and the children of Judah are oppressed together; and all that took them captive hold them fast; they refuse to let them go.

units.leftText: Their Redeemer is strong; the LORD of Hosts is His name. He will fervently plead their case so that He may bring rest to the earth, but turmoil to those who live in Babylon.
units.rightText: Their Redeemer is strong; Jehovah of hosts is his name: he will thoroughly plead their cause, that he may give rest to the earth, and disquiet the inhabitants of Babylon.

units.leftText: A sword is against the Chaldeans, declares the LORD, against those who live in Babylon, and against her officials and wise men.
units.rightText: A sword is upon the Chaldeans, saith Jehovah, and upon the inhabitants of Babylon, and upon her princes, and upon her wise men.

units.leftText: A sword is against her false prophets, and they will become fools. A sword is against her warriors, and they will be filled with terror.
units.rightText: A sword is upon the boasters, and they shall become fools; a sword is upon her mighty men, and they shall be dismayed.

units.leftText: A sword is against her horses and chariots and against all the foreigners in her midst, and they will become like women. A sword is against her treasuries, and they will be plundered.
units.rightText: A sword is upon their horses, and upon their chariots, and upon all the mingled people that are in the midst of her; and they shall become as women: a sword is upon her treasures, and they shall be robbed.

units.leftText: A drought is upon her waters, and they will be dried up. For it is a land of graven images, and the people go mad over idols.
units.rightText: A drought is upon her waters, and they shall be dried up; for it is a land of graven images, and they are mad over idols.
leftNotes: 50:38 Or go mad with fear

units.leftText: So the desert creatures and hyenas will live there and ostriches will dwell there. It will never again be inhabited or lived in from generation to generation.
units.rightText: Therefore the wild beasts of the desert with the wolves shall dwell there, and the ostriches shall dwell therein: and it shall be no more inhabited for ever; neither shall it be dwelt in from generation to generation.
leftNotes: 50:39 Literally daughters of an ostrich or daughters of an owl

units.leftText: As God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah along with their neighbors,” declares the LORD, “no one will dwell there; no man will abide there.
units.rightText: As when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and the neighbor cities thereof, saith Jehovah, so shall no man dwell there, neither shall any son of man sojourn therein.

units.leftText: Behold, an army is coming from the north; a great nation and many kings are stirred up from the ends of the earth.
units.rightText: Behold, a people cometh from the north; and a great nation and many kings shall be stirred up from the uttermost parts of the earth.

units.leftText: They grasp the bow and spear; they are cruel and merciless. Their voice roars like the sea, and they ride upon horses, lined up like men in formation against you, O Daughter of Babylon.
units.rightText: They lay hold on bow and spear; they are cruel, and have no mercy; their voice roareth like the sea; and they ride upon horses, every one set in array, as a man to the battle, against thee, O daughter of Babylon.
leftNotes: 50:42 Or javelin

units.leftText: The king of Babylon has heard the report, and his hands hang limp. Anguish has gripped him, pain like that of a woman in labor.
units.rightText: The king of Babylon hath heard the tidings of them, and his hands wax feeble: anguish hath taken hold of him, and pangs as of a woman in travail.

units.leftText: Behold, one will come up like a lion from the thickets of the Jordan to the watered pasture. For in an instant I will chase Babylon from her land. Who is the chosen one I will appoint for this? For who is like Me, and who can challenge Me? What shepherd can stand against Me?”
units.rightText: Behold, the enemy shall come up like a lion from the pride of the Jordan against the strong habitation: for I will suddenly make them run away from it; and whoso is chosen, him will I appoint over it: for who is like me? and who will appoint me a time? and who is the shepherd that can stand before me?

units.leftText: Therefore hear the plans that the LORD has drawn up against Babylon and the strategies He has devised against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely the little ones of the flock will be dragged away; certainly their pasture will be made desolate because of them.
units.rightText: Therefore hear ye the counsel of Jehovah, that he hath taken against Babylon; and his purposes, that he hath purposed against the land of the Chaldeans: Surely they shall drag them away, even the little ones of the flock; surely he shall make their habitation desolate over them.

units.leftText: At the sound of Babylon’s capture the earth will quake; a cry will be heard among the nations.
units.rightText: At the noise of the taking of Babylon the earth trembleth, and the cry is heard among the nations.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “Behold, I will stir up against Babylon and against the people of Leb-kamai the spirit of a destroyer.
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah: Behold, I will raise up against Babylon, and against them that dwell in Leb-kamai, a destroying wind.
leftNotes: 51:1 Leb-kamai is a code name for Chaldea, that is, Babylonia.

units.leftText: I will send strangers to Babylon to winnow her and empty her land; for they will come against her from every side in her day of disaster.
units.rightText: And I will send unto Babylon strangers, that shall winnow her; and they shall empty her land: for in the day of trouble they shall be against her round about.

units.leftText: Do not let the archer bend his bow or put on his armor. Do not spare her young men; devote all her army to destruction!
units.rightText: Against him that bendeth let the archer bend his bow, and against him that lifteth himself up in his coat of mail: and spare ye not her young men; destroy ye utterly all her host.
leftNotes: 51:3 Forms of the Hebrew cherem refer to the giving over of things or persons to the LORD, either by destroying them or by giving them as an offering.

units.leftText: And they will fall slain in the land of the Chaldeans, and pierced through in her streets.
units.rightText: And they shall fall down slain in the land of the Chaldeans, and thrust through in her streets.
leftNotes: 51:4 That is, the Babylonians; also in verse 54

units.leftText: For Israel and Judah have not been abandoned by their God, the LORD of Hosts, though their land is full of guilt before the Holy One of Israel.”
units.rightText: For Israel is not forsaken, nor Judah, of his God, of Jehovah of hosts; though their land is full of guilt against the Holy One of Israel.

units.leftText: Flee from Babylon! Escape with your lives! Do not be destroyed in her punishment. For this is the time of the LORD’s vengeance; He will pay her what she deserves.
units.rightText: Flee out of the midst of Babylon, and save every man his life; be not cut off in her iniquity: for it is the time of Jehovah’s vengeance; he will render unto her a recompense.

units.leftText: Babylon was a gold cup in the hand of the LORD, making the whole earth drunk. The nations drank her wine; therefore the nations have gone mad.
units.rightText: Babylon hath been a golden cup in Jehovah’s hand, that made all the earth drunken: the nations have drunk of her wine; therefore the nations are mad.

units.leftText: Suddenly Babylon has fallen and been shattered. Wail for her; get her balm for her pain; perhaps she can be healed.
units.rightText: Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed: wail for her; take balm for her pain, if so be she may be healed.

units.leftText: “We tried to heal Babylon, but she could not be healed. Abandon her! Let each of us go to his own land, for her judgment extends to the sky and reaches to the clouds.”
units.rightText: We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed: forsake her, and let us go every one into his own country; for her judgment reacheth unto heaven, and is lifted up even to the skies.

units.leftText: “The LORD has brought forth our vindication; come, let us tell in Zion what the LORD our God has accomplished.”
units.rightText: Jehovah hath brought forth our righteousness: come, and let us declare in Zion the work of Jehovah our God.

units.leftText: Sharpen the arrows! Fill the quivers! The LORD has aroused the spirit of the kings of the Medes, because His plan is aimed at Babylon to destroy her, for it is the vengeance of the LORD — vengeance for His temple.
units.rightText: Make sharp the arrows; hold firm the shields: Jehovah hath stirred up the spirit of the kings of the Medes; because his purpose is against Babylon, to destroy it: for it is the vengeance of Jehovah, the vengeance of his temple.
leftNotes: 51:11 LXX and some translations of the Hebrew; literally Fill the hand with the shields! or Take up the shields!

units.leftText: Raise a banner against the walls of Babylon; post the guard; station the watchmen; prepare the ambush. For the LORD has both devised and accomplished what He spoke against the people of Babylon.
units.rightText: Set up a standard against the walls of Babylon, make the watch strong, set the watchmen, prepare the ambushes; for Jehovah hath both purposed and done that which he spake concerning the inhabitants of Babylon.

units.leftText: You who dwell by many waters, rich in treasures, your end has come; the thread of your life is cut.
units.rightText: O thou that dwellest upon many waters, abundant in treasures, thine end is come, the measure of thy covetousness.

units.leftText: The LORD of Hosts has sworn by Himself: “Surely I will fill you up with men as with locusts, and they will shout in triumph over you.” Praise to the God of Jacob (Isaiah 25:1–12|ISA 25:1-12*)
units.rightText: Jehovah of hosts hath sworn by himself, saying, Surely I will fill thee with men, as with the canker-worm; and they shall lift up a shout against thee.

units.leftText: The LORD made the earth by His power; He established the world by His wisdom and stretched out the heavens by His understanding.
units.rightText: He hath made the earth by his power, he hath established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding hath he stretched out the heavens.

units.leftText: When He thunders, the waters in the heavens roar; He causes the clouds to rise from the ends of the earth. He generates the lightning with the rain and brings forth the wind from His storehouses.
units.rightText: When he uttereth his voice, there is a tumult of waters in the heavens, and he causeth the vapors to ascend from the ends of the earth; he maketh lightnings for the rain, and bringeth forth the wind out of his treasuries.

units.leftText: Every man is senseless and devoid of knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idols. For his molten images are a fraud, and there is no breath in them.
units.rightText: Every man is become brutish and is without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his image; for his molten image is falsehood, and there is no breath in them.

units.leftText: They are worthless, a work to be mocked. In the time of their punishment they will perish.
units.rightText: They are vanity, a work of delusion: in the time of their visitation they shall perish.

units.leftText: The Portion of Jacob is not like these, for He is the Maker of all things, and of the tribe of His inheritance — the LORD of Hosts is His name. Babylon’s Punishment
units.rightText: The portion of Jacob is not like these; for he is the former of all things; and Israel is the tribe of his inheritance: Jehovah of hosts is his name.

units.leftText: “You are My war club, My weapon for battle. With you I shatter nations; with you I bring kingdoms to ruin.
units.rightText: Thou art my battle-axe and weapons of war: and with thee will I break in pieces the nations; and with thee will I destroy kingdoms;

units.leftText: With you I shatter the horse and rider; with you I shatter the chariot and driver.
units.rightText: and with thee will I break in pieces the horse and his rider;

units.leftText: With you I shatter man and woman; with you I shatter the old man and the youth; with you I shatter the young man and the maiden.
units.rightText: and with thee will I break in pieces the chariot and him that rideth therein; and with thee will I break in pieces man and woman; and with thee will I break in pieces the old man and the youth; and with thee will I break in pieces the young man and the virgin;

units.leftText: With you I shatter the shepherd and his flock; with you I shatter the farmer and his oxen; with you I shatter the governors and officials.
units.rightText: and with thee will I break in pieces the shepherd and his flock; and with thee will I break in pieces the husbandman and his yoke of oxen; and with thee will I break in pieces governors and deputies.

units.leftText: Before your very eyes I will repay Babylon and all the dwellers of Chaldea for all the evil they have done in Zion,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: And I will render unto Babylon and to all the inhabitants of Chaldea all their evil that they have done in Zion in your sight, saith Jehovah.
leftNotes: 51:24 That is, Babylonia; also in verse 35

units.leftText: “Behold, I am against you, O destroying mountain, you who devastate the whole earth, declares the LORD. I will stretch out My hand against you; I will roll you over the cliffs and turn you into a charred mountain.
units.rightText: Behold, I am against thee, O destroying mountain, saith Jehovah, which destroyest all the earth; and I will stretch out my hand upon thee, and roll thee down from the rocks, and will make thee a burnt mountain.

units.leftText: No one shall retrieve from you a cornerstone or a foundation stone, because you will become desolate forever,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: And they shall not take of thee a stone for a corner, nor a stone for foundations; but thou shalt be desolate for ever, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Raise a banner in the land! Blow the ram’s horn among the nations! Prepare the nations against her. Summon the kingdoms against her — Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Appoint a captain against her; bring up horses like swarming locusts.
units.rightText: Set ye up a standard in the land, blow the trumpet among the nations, prepare the nations against her, call together against her the kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz: appoint a marshal against her; cause the horses to come up as the rough canker-worm.

units.leftText: Prepare the nations for battle against her — the kings of the Medes, their governors and all their officials, and all the lands they rule.
units.rightText: Prepare against her the nations, the kings of the Medes, the governors thereof, and all the deputies thereof, and all the land of their dominion.

units.leftText: The earth quakes and writhes because the LORD’s intentions against Babylon stand: to make the land of Babylon a desolation, without inhabitant.
units.rightText: And the land trembleth and is in pain; for the purposes of Jehovah against Babylon do stand, to make the land of Babylon a desolation, without inhabitant.

units.leftText: The warriors of Babylon have stopped fighting; they sit in their strongholds. Their strength is exhausted; they have become like women. Babylon’s homes have been set ablaze, the bars of her gates are broken.
units.rightText: The mighty men of Babylon have forborne to fight, they remain in their strongholds; their might hath failed; they are become as women: her dwelling-places are set on fire; her bars are broken.

units.leftText: One courier races to meet another, and messenger follows messenger, to announce to the king of Babylon that his city has been captured from end to end.
units.rightText: One post shall run to meet another, and one messenger to meet another, to show the king of Babylon that his city is taken on every quarter:

units.leftText: The fords have been seized, the marshes set on fire, and the soldiers are terrified.”
units.rightText: and the passages are seized, and the reeds they have burned with fire, and the men of war are affrighted.

units.leftText: For this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: “The Daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trampled. In just a little while her harvest time will come.”
units.rightText: For thus saith Jehovah of hosts, the God of Israel: The daughter of Babylon is like a threshing-floor at the time when it is trodden; yet a little while, and the time of harvest shall come for her.

units.leftText: “Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured me; he has crushed me. He has set me aside like an empty vessel; he has swallowed me like a monster; he filled his belly with my delicacies and vomited me out.
units.rightText: Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon hath devoured me, he hath crushed me, he hath made me an empty vessel, he hath, like a monster, swallowed me up, he hath filled his maw with my delicacies; he hath cast me out.
leftNotes: 51:34 Or expelled me

units.leftText: May the violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon,” says the dweller of Zion. “May my blood be on the dwellers of Chaldea,” says Jerusalem.
units.rightText: The violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon, shall the inhabitant of Zion say; and, My blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea, shall Jerusalem say.

units.leftText: Therefore this is what the LORD says: “Behold, I will plead your case and take vengeance on your behalf; I will dry up her sea and make her springs run dry.
units.rightText: Therefore thus saith Jehovah: Behold, I will plead thy cause, and take vengeance for thee; and I will dry up her sea, and make her fountain dry.

units.leftText: Babylon will become a heap of rubble, a haunt for jackals, an object of horror and scorn, without inhabitant.
units.rightText: And Babylon shall become heaps, a dwelling-place for jackals, an astonishment, and a hissing, without inhabitant.
leftNotes: 51:37 Or serpents or dragons

units.leftText: They will roar together like young lions; they will growl like lion cubs.
units.rightText: They shall roar together like young lions; they shall growl as lions’ whelps.

units.leftText: While they are flushed with heat, I will serve them a feast, and I will make them drunk so that they may revel; then they will fall asleep forever and never wake up, declares the LORD.
units.rightText: When they are heated, I will make their feast, and I will make them drunken, that they may rejoice, and sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with male goats.
units.rightText: I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams with he-goats.

units.leftText: How Sheshach has been captured! The praise of all the earth has been seized. What a horror Babylon has become among the nations!
units.rightText: How is Sheshach taken! and the praise of the whole earth seized! how is Babylon become a desolation among the nations!
leftNotes: 51:41 Sheshach is a code name for Babylon.

units.leftText: The sea has come up over Babylon; she is covered in turbulent waves.
units.rightText: The sea is come up upon Babylon; she is covered with the multitude of the waves thereof.

units.leftText: Her cities have become a desolation, a dry and arid land, a land where no one lives, where no son of man passes through.
units.rightText: Her cities are become a desolation, a dry land, and a desert, a land wherein no man dwelleth, neither doth any son of man pass thereby.

units.leftText: I will punish Bel in Babylon. I will make him spew out what he swallowed. The nations will no longer stream to him; even the wall of Babylon will fall.
units.rightText: And I will execute judgment upon Bel in Babylon, and I will bring forth out of his mouth that which he hath swallowed up; and the nations shall not flow any more unto him: yea, the wall of Babylon shall fall.

units.leftText: Come out of her, My people! Save your lives, each of you, from the fierce anger of the LORD.
units.rightText: My people, go ye out of the midst of her, and save yourselves every man from the fierce anger of Jehovah.
leftNotes: 51:45 See Revelation 18:4|REV 18:4*.

units.leftText: Do not let your heart grow faint, and do not be afraid when the rumor is heard in the land; for a rumor will come one year— and then another the next year— of violence in the land and of ruler against ruler.
units.rightText: And let not your heart faint, neither fear ye for the tidings that shall be heard in the land; for tidings shall come one year, and after that in another year shall come tidings, and violence in the land, ruler against ruler.

units.leftText: Therefore, behold, the days are coming when I will punish the idols of Babylon. Her entire land will suffer shame, and all her slain will lie fallen within her.
units.rightText: Therefore, behold, the days come, that I will execute judgment upon the graven images of Babylon; and her whole land shall be confounded; and all her slain shall fall in the midst of her.

units.leftText: Then heaven and earth and all that is in them will shout for joy over Babylon because the destroyers from the north will come against her,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: Then the heavens and the earth, and all that is therein, shall sing for joy over Babylon; for the destroyers shall come unto her from the north, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Babylon must fall on account of the slain of Israel, just as the slain of all the earth have fallen because of Babylon.
units.rightText: As Babylon hath caused the slain of Israel to fall, so at Babylon shall fall the slain of all the land.

units.leftText: You who have escaped the sword, depart and do not linger! Remember the LORD from far away, and let Jerusalem come to mind.”
units.rightText: Ye that have escaped the sword, go ye, stand not still; remember Jehovah from afar, and let Jerusalem come into your mind.

units.leftText: “We are ashamed because we have heard reproach; disgrace has covered our faces, because foreigners have entered the holy places of the LORD’s house.”
units.rightText: We are confounded, because we have heard reproach; confusion hath covered our faces: for strangers are come into the sanctuaries of Jehovah’s house.

units.leftText: “Therefore, behold, the days are coming,” declares the LORD, “when I will punish her idols, and throughout her land the wounded will groan.
units.rightText: Wherefore, behold, the days come, saith Jehovah, that I will execute judgment upon her graven images; and through all her land the wounded shall groan.

units.leftText: Even if Babylon ascends to the heavens and fortifies her lofty stronghold, the destroyers I send will come against her,” declares the LORD.
units.rightText: Though Babylon should mount up to heaven, and though she should fortify the height of her strength, yet from me shall destroyers come unto her, saith Jehovah.

units.leftText: “The sound of a cry comes from Babylon, the sound of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!
units.rightText: The sound of a cry from Babylon, and of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans!

units.leftText: For the LORD will destroy Babylon; He will silence her mighty voice. The waves will roar like great waters; the tumult of their voices will resound.
units.rightText: For Jehovah layeth Babylon waste, and destroyeth out of her the great voice; and their waves roar like many waters; the noise of their voice is uttered:

units.leftText: For a destroyer is coming against her — against Babylon. Her warriors will be captured, and their bows will be broken, for the LORD is a God of retribution; He will repay in full.
units.rightText: for the destroyer is come upon her, even upon Babylon, and her mighty men are taken, their bows are broken in pieces; for Jehovah is a God of recompenses, he will surely requite.

units.leftText: I will make her princes and wise men drunk, along with her governors, officials, and warriors. Then they will fall asleep forever and not wake up,” declares the King, whose name is the LORD of Hosts.
units.rightText: And I will make drunk her princes and her wise men, her governors and her deputies, and her mighty men; and they shall sleep a perpetual sleep, and not wake, saith the King, whose name is Jehovah of hosts.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Babylon’s thick walls will be leveled, and her high gates consumed by fire. So the labor of the people will be for nothing; the nations will exhaust themselves to fuel the flames.” Jeremiah’s Message to Seraiah
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah of hosts: The broad walls of Babylon shall be utterly overthrown, and her high gates shall be burned with fire; and the peoples shall labor for vanity, and the nations for the fire; and they shall be weary.

units.leftText: This is the message that Jeremiah the prophet gave to the quartermaster Seraiah son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, when he went to Babylon with King Zedekiah of Judah in the fourth year of Zedekiah’s reign.
